author: Dower, John W.
title: War Without Mercy: Race and Power in the Pacific War
notes: The reason this arc cannot be told as a sequence of landings. Dower reads the propaganda, the cartoons, the training material and the private language of both sides and shows a war conducted by each as against a race rather than a state — the American 'exterminationist' rhetoric and the Japanese doctrine of purity together, which is the point: it is not a book about one side's racism. It is what the packs draw on for why prisoners were rarely taken, why surrender was rare, and why the casualty arithmetic of 1945 was argued the way it was. It is an argument and is cited as one, beside the operational sources rather than instead of them. Verified against catalogue records only; no ISBN is recorded.
